app.name: AwakeTab
app.tagline: The tab that keeps your screen awake.

home.title: Keep Your Screen Awake — AwakeTab
home.description: Keep your screen awake in this browser tab with the Wake Lock API. Honest status, presets, until-time. No account.
home.intro: AwakeTab uses the browser's Wake Lock API while this tab is visible, and its status only says the screen is awake after the browser confirms the lock.

uses.title: What are you keeping awake?
uses.lead: Each one opens the tool already set for the job, with the length it needs.

cooking.body: The recipe stays lit while your hands are floury, with kitchen timers beside it.

reading.body: A long article stays on screen while you read, with no tap to wake it.

presentations.body: Set it to the end of your talk and keep it in a floating window beside the slides.

dashboards.body: A wall screen stays on all day, and a link can start the session as the page loads.

videoCalls.body: The display stays on when the video pauses. Your chat status is left alone.

downloads.body: The screen stays on through a long download, and a visible tab holds off idle sleep.

final.title: One tap, and the screen stays on.
final.body: The pill says {held} only after the browser confirms the lock. For a hidden tab or a minimised window, the extension keeps going.
final.docs: How it works, limits and FAQ in the docs

yours.title: Make it yours
yours.lead: Clock faces, colours, backgrounds, focus sounds and a notepad. Each one loads only when you pick it, and the status pill still tells you the truth.

faces.title: Twelve clock faces
faces.body: Classic, retro and modern. Every face shows your session, follows your lamp colour and knows when the screen is paused. Swipe the clock or press C to switch.

looks.title: Themes, lamps and backgrounds
looks.body: Clear Night, Paper and Nord, four lamps, three backgrounds and three presets are free. Pro adds six themes, eight lamps, a colour of your own, five backgrounds and five presets.
looks.themes: Colour themes, each with a light and a dark version
looks.tryNote: Any Pro look can be tried for 5 minutes, as often as you like. Nothing is saved.

sound.title: Sounds for focus
sound.body: Seven focus sounds made live in your browser, five end sounds, vibration and a quiet tick-tock, all free. Pro adds a mixer to layer them.
sound.honest: Nothing plays until you ask, and sound never keeps the screen awake.

notes.title: A notepad beside the clock
notes.body: Checklists, headings, export and voice typing. Notes stay in this browser and work offline. One note is free; Pro keeps as many as you like.

focus.title: Focus tools
focus.body: A Pomodoro with pause and skip, an intention under the clock, a breathing guide and a second time zone. With Pro the Pomodoro repeats on its own.

ext.title: Keep the screen awake with the tab out of sight
ext.lead: The extension asks the browser itself to keep the screen awake, so it keeps going behind other windows.

hidden.title: Tab hidden or window minimised
hidden.body: It keeps going while the browser is running.

system.title: Only the system, if you prefer
system.body: System level keeps the computer awake and lets the screen dim or turn off.

badge.title: Status in the toolbar
badge.body: The badge shows ON, SYS or the minutes left.

shortcut.title: A shortcut from any tab

levels.title: Choose your level
levels.lead: Keeping a screen awake is free, in this tab and in the extension, and so are every clock face and focus sound. Pro adds more looks, a sound mixer, more notes and a longer memory.

faq.q1: Does Pro keep the screen awake better?
faq.a1: No. Free and Pro use the same wake lock and the same status pill. Pro adds looks, a sound mixer, more notes, a repeating Pomodoro, a message, history and schedules on top.
faq.a2: No. Polar handles checkout and emails you a licence key. AwakeTab never stores a password.
faq.a3: Each browser where you enter the key uses one of five activations. AwakeTab for Chrome activates itself and uses one too. Devices unused for 90 days are removed automatically when you activate a new one.
faq.q5: Can I try Pro before paying?
faq.a5: Yes. In the tool, every Pro theme, lamp, background and preset, the sound mixer, more notes, the repeating Pomodoro and a shared Message link can be tried for 5 minutes, as often as you like. A small bar counts down, then the tool goes back to your free choice, and nothing is saved. After you pay, the 14-day refund still applies.
faq.q6: What happens if my yearly plan ends?
faq.a6: Pro features switch off and the free tool keeps working. Your settings stay, and stats older than 7 days are hidden, not deleted. Renew and they come back.
faq.a7: No. Pro is {yearly} a year, or one payment with no renewal. Both cover 5 devices.

extension.title: Chrome extension to keep your screen awake — AwakeTab
extension.description: AwakeTab for Chrome keeps your screen or computer awake from the toolbar, even when the tab is hidden. Timers, schedules, an honest status and no tracking.
extension.lead: The web app can hold a wake lock only while its tab is visible. The extension asks Chrome itself to keep the display awake, or just the computer, so it keeps working when the tab is hidden or the window is minimised.

cta.pending: The listing is waiting for store review, so for now these buttons open a store search.

firefox.title: Using Firefox or Safari?
firefox.body: Firefox and Safari don’t give extensions a power API, so there is no AwakeTab extension for them. The web app keeps the screen awake while its tab is visible.

features.title: What it does
features.levels: Screen or System: keep the display on, or keep only the computer awake and let the screen dim.
features.timers: The same presets as the web app — 15 minutes to 4 hours, until a time, or until you stop.
features.badge: The toolbar badge shows ON, SYS or the minutes left, and Alt+Shift+A toggles it from any tab.
features.pro: With Pro: weekly schedules, and auto-start when Chrome opens or when you visit a site you choose.

limits.running: It works only while Chrome is running.
limits.lid: It can’t stop sleep when you close a laptop lid.
limits.presence: It doesn’t keep Teams or Slack showing you as available: presence follows your keyboard and mouse, and AwakeTab never fakes input.

permissions.title: Permissions, and why
permissions.power: power — hold the display or system keep-awake.
permissions.storage: storage — save your settings and the current session.
permissions.alarms: alarms — run timers and schedules while the background worker sleeps.
permissions.notifications: notifications (optional) — tell you when a timer ends.
permissions.sites: Site access (optional, one site at a time) — start automatically on sites you pick. No site access by default.
permissions.lead: Three it needs to work, two you can turn on. It gets no site access unless you pick a site.

extension.privacy: Anonymous usage statistics are off by default. The extension never sends URLs, tab titles or site names, and it shows no ads.
extension.web: Rather not install anything? The web app keeps the screen awake while its tab is visible.
extension.value: Keeps your screen awake from the toolbar, even when the tab is hidden or the window is minimised.

fact.hidden: Keeps going with the tab hidden
fact.private: No ads, no site access by default

alt.why: Why there is no extension for this browser

install.title: Install
install.body: Add it from the Chrome Web Store, or from Edge Add-ons in Edge.

pin.title: Pin it
pin.body: Open the Extensions menu (the puzzle piece) and pin AwakeTab, so its badge stays in view.

press.title: Press the shortcut
press.body: From any tab, it starts your usual length. Press it again to stop. On a Mac, Alt is the Option key.

faq.title: Questions
faq.a1: Yes. Timers, Screen or System, the toolbar badge and the shortcut are free. Pro adds weekly schedules and auto-start.
faq.q2: Can it see the sites I visit?
faq.a2: No. It has no site access by default and never sends URLs, tab titles or site names. Auto-start on a site, a Pro feature, asks for access to that one site.
faq.q3: Why not just use the web app?
faq.a3: The web app keeps the screen awake only while its tab is visible. The extension keeps going while you work in other tabs or with the window minimised, as long as Chrome is running.
faq.a4: Yes. Open chrome://extensions/shortcuts in Chrome, or edge://extensions/shortcuts in Edge, and set your own. Do that too if another extension already uses Alt+Shift+A.
faq.q5: Does the extension have the clock faces, sounds and notes?
faq.a5: No, those live in the web app. The extension keeps the screen, or only the computer, awake from the toolbar. Open AwakeTab from its pop-up for the twelve clock faces, colour themes, focus sounds, the notepad and the focus tools.

why.title: How AwakeTab knows
why.timerD: Counts on your system clock, so a laptop that slept comes back with an honest number, not a stale one.
why.powerD: Browsers do not report them. On iPhone, Low Power Mode forces a 30-second Auto-Lock even while the pill says awake.
why.tabVisible: Visible. If you switch away, the browser takes the lock back and the pill says so.
why.lockReady: Not requested yet. Nothing is keeping the screen on until you tap Keep awake.
why.tabReady: Browsers grant a wake lock only to a visible tab.
why.lockEnded: Released at {time} when the session ended. The screen can sleep now.
why.lockStarting: Asked your browser at {time}. Waiting for its answer.
why.lockPaused: Released by the browser at {time}, when this tab was hidden. The screen may sleep.
why.tabPaused: Hidden. Come back and AwakeTab asks for the lock again by itself.
why.lockBlocked: Refused by the browser at {time}. Nothing is keeping the screen on right now.
why.causesD: The tab was not in front, Safari needs one tap first, or Firefox is on 5% battery or less. The fix is below.
why.lockNone: This browser has no Screen Wake Lock API, so there is nothing to ask for.
why.videoTap: Ready, but it needs one tap before it can play. It needs this tab visible and uses a little more battery.
why.videoOn: A muted one-frame video is playing, which keeps the screen on. It needs this tab visible and uses a little more battery.
why.tabVideo: Visible. The video stops when the tab is hidden, and the pill will say so.
why.lockHeld: Held. Your browser confirmed it at {time} and has not taken it back since.

blurb.ring: The signature. The lamp rides the end of the arc and turns amber the moment the lock pauses.
blurb.bold: Heavy display digits for across-the-room reading, with a slim progress rail.
blurb.horizon: A lamp-sun sets toward the horizon as the session runs down.
blurb.tide: The water level is the time left. Calm and glanceable.
blurb.flip: Split-flap cards with a real hinge gap.
blurb.rolling: Odometer drums — the next digit is always just visible.
blurb.analog: Real time on the hands; the lamp arc on the bezel runs to the end time.
blurb.luxe: A deeper dial with serif numerals, a minute track and a lamp sector.
blurb.rings: Session, minutes and seconds as three concentric rings.
blurb.words: Time in a sentence, written natively in each of the eight languages.
blurb.nixie: Glass tubes with mesh and ghost 8s; the glow takes the lamp colour.
blurb.lcd: Slanted segments over a faint 88:88 ghost, like a bedside clock.
blurb.led: Dot-matrix board with a scrolling status line. Best in OLED.
blurb.dive: A dive-watch bezel: the green arc is the minutes left, the hands keep real time.
blurb.chrono: Minute and second sub-dials with a sweeping chrono hand.
blurb.gauge: An instrument needle with a five-minute warning zone.
blurb.type: Minutes in huge type, seconds in green, a progress hairline.
blurb.bars: The whole session as bars — spent fades, the current one breathes.
blurb.timeline: Now → Ends, like a boarding pass. The most literal way to read time left.
blurb.pilot: Aviator dial with a triangle at 12, sword hands and a green minutes-left sector.
blurb.dual: Two small dials side by side: the time now and the time it ends.
blurb.radar: A sweeping scope; the blip marks the end time on the rings.
blurb.dots: Sixty dots around the dial; each minute left keeps one lit.
blurb.hourglass: Sand falls from top to bottom as the session runs; a fine stream moves while awake.
blurb.battery: Time left as a charge level, with a gentle sheen across the cell.
blurb.stack: Minutes over seconds in a tight editorial stack, end time underneath.
blurb.board: Split-flap tiles like a station board; the seconds tile flaps each tick.
blurb.orbit: Three orbits: the session in green, minutes in sky, a violet moon sweeping the seconds.
blurb.disc: A solid disc that shrinks toward 12, warming from green to ember in the last minutes.
blurb.clocks: Twenty-four tiny clocks whose hands swing into place to spell the time left.
blurb.wordgrid: A letter grid that lights the words — “about forty minutes left”.
blurb.tape: A minute ruler glides under a fixed needle; the heat strip shows the final stretch.
blurb.moon: The moon wanes from full to new as the session runs down, under an aurora sky.

1.body: 15 minutes, an hour, until a time — or no end at all.

2.body: Your browser’s Screen Wake Lock keeps the display on.

3.body: A soft chime when time’s up; the screen sleeps normally again.

limits.title: Honest about limits
limits.body: A browser can keep the screen on, not the whole computer. Battery saver, closing the lid or a company lock policy can still win — AwakeTab tells you when that happens and how to fix it.

1._: Does it work on iPhone and iPad?
1.a: Yes, in Safari on iOS and iPadOS 16.4 or later. Older versions use a silent video fallback.

2.a: No. Settings stay on this device. Pro uses an account only to sync your devices.

3._: Will it stop my work laptop from locking?
3.a: It keeps the display awake while the tab is open. Company lock policies still apply, and they should.

4.a: Keeping awake is free. Pro adds device sync, full history and the sound mixer.

embedPage.lead: Add a Cook Mode button that keeps your readers' screens awake: one script tag, an honest status and no third-party requests. Free with a credit link.
embedPage.builderSub: Pick how it looks. The demo and the snippet change as you go.
embedPage.demoNote: This is the real widget, with the credit line the loader adds under it.
embedPage.snippetNote: Paste it where the widget should appear. The loader adds the credit link itself.
embedPage.allowBody: Browsers let an embedded page keep the screen awake only when the site allows it with allow="screen-wake-lock". The loader always adds it. If your platform strips script tags, paste this iframe instead and keep the allow attribute.
embedPage.apiBody: The loader exposes window.AwakeTabEmbed with on("state", callback), start({ preset, ms, until }), stop() and setTheme(theme). Call start() from a click: the video fallback needs a tap.
embedPage.licenceBody: A Business licence will remove the credit line and give the Start button your brand colour. Keeping the screen awake is the same either way.
